Subject: EU node provisioning + APAC standby capacity — renewal top-up discussion

Hi Lars / Brightwell ops team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As Brightwell approaches renewal (Dec 1), we wanted to surface a short proposal for the region expansion items we discussed so they can be incorporated into the renewal amendment and SOW. High-level: add a dedicated EU onshore serving node (single-tenant pool) and an APAC warm-standby pool for burst/failover during business hours.

Why this helps Brightwell:
- EU onshore node: ensures EU data residency for European patients and reduces cross-region latency for EU users.
- APAC warm-standby: provides a low-cost hot-path for burst traffic and a failover lane if EU capacity is saturated or during maintenance.

Proposed commercial changes (draft):
- Term: extend current contract by 12 months from Dec 1, 2027.
- Capacity top-up: EU node: 2 x p4-equivalent reserved units; APAC standby: 1 x p4-equivalent warm standby (billed at reduced standby rate with burst billing).
- One-time SOW fee for provisioning/onboarding and runbook validation: see attached SOW v2.
- Credit request: Brightwell asked about a 10% uplift credit to help transition. We can evaluate based on final committed UCapacity.

Attachments: draft_sow_brightwell_v2.pdf (PDF, draft), residency_matrix_brightwell.csv (CSV)

Next steps: can you confirm the residency must include "onshore keying" (KMS/HSM in EU) vs. "onshore processing only"? Also confirm procurement timeline so we can align a provisioning window in late Jan.

Happy to jump on a short call this week if that helps.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0198

Thanks — this looks helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
1) Residency: we require EU onshore keying (we need customer-managed KMS in an EU region or HSM integration). Processing in EU is mandatory as well.
2) Cutover window: procurement expects to sign the renewal by mid-Nov if the SOW/terms are acceptable; target provisioning late Jan is fine but we need a canary cutover earlier (Feb 1) for a pilot with 10% traffic.
3) Compliance artifacts: please provide SOC2 Type II and a summary of data flows for EU nodes.

Also looping our procurement contact for commercial terms. We have an internal budget cadence on Oct 25 — can Redwood provide a final priced SOW by Oct 20?
